messages:
Anika R.: Heads-up — onboarding sample failing under strict typecheckers. Generated models in python-sdk v0.9.2 annotate most response fields as `Any` and stream chunks come through as raw `dict`. Minimal repro:
```py
resp = await client.chat.create(prompt="hello")
# mypy/pyright: accessing resp.output[0].text -> "Item has type Any" / "Property 'text' does not exist on type 'Any'"

async for chunk in client.chat.stream(prompt="hi"):
    print(chunk['text'])  # pyright: Property 'text' does not exist on type 'dict'
```

Tom S.: Yep saw that. We intentionally kept runtime shapes flexible for perf, but typing noise is a big DX hit for new hires and example apps.

Priya S.: Two quick asks from our side: 1) typed params on client methods (e.g., `temperature: float | None`, `max_tokens: int | None`) so typecheckers catch obvious mistakes, and 2) a tiny TypedDict for streaming chunks (TypedChunk) so editor completions and pyright stop complaining.

Sam (sdk): Agreed on both. Proposed plan:
- Generate a generic `Response[T]` and annotate non-streaming methods as `-> Response[Model]`
- Emit shallow `TypedDict` for stream events: `TypedChunk = TypedDict('TypedChunk', {'text': Optional[str], 'role': Optional[str], 'delta': Optional[dict]})` and type streams as `AsyncIterator[TypedChunk]`
- Generate `.pyi` stubs for the public surface so strict checkers get good signatures without heavy runtime parsing
- Add client flags to opt out: `typed_responses: bool = True` and `return_raw_stream: bool = False`
- Map nullable -> `Optional[...]`, oneOf -> `Union[...]` when safe, and primitive mappings `number->float`, `integer->int`, `boolean->bool`, `string->str`

Anika R.: Nice. The `.pyi` approach is appealing — teams that care about perf can keep runtime behavior but still vendor stubs in CI. Please ensure overloads cover sync/async variants.

Tom S.: Also please include minimal examples in `examples/typed_chat.py` and `examples/typed_stream.py` that are clean under mypy and pyright. We should add a lightweight CI job that typechecks `examples/` with a recommended config. That will catch regressions before they break onboarding.

Priya S.: One more: pydantic compatibility. Some customers are on v1 and others on v2. Generator should emit a small shim or guard so imports don't blow up. Document minimum supported pydantic in README and add a migration note.

Sam (sdk): Will do. Implementation notes: shallow conversion for streaming (no full pydantic validation per chunk), `.pyi` stubgen will be best-effort and generated alongside code, and we'll default to `typed_responses=True` but document opt-out. We'll include `Literal[...]` where enum-like values are present for better editor completions.

lint-bot: Created issue SDK-3005: "python-sdk: improve typings — .pyi stubgen, Response[T], TypedChunk, stricter param annotations, examples CI" assigned to @sam_sdk

Anika R.: Thanks — small wins (param typing + TypedDict for stream) will already reduce a lot of noise. Happy to review the examples/PR.

Sam (sdk): I'll open a draft PR with generator template changes, two example files, and a tiny `.pyi` emitter. Targeting a 0.9.x patch for param fixes and shallow TypedDicts, and 0.10.0-alpha for full stubgen + examples CI. Will ping here when the draft lands.

Priya S.: Please CC devex on the PR so we can update onboarding checklist and sample-app templates. Also include a short migration section that explains the opt-out flags and how to vendor stubs-only for CI.

Tom S.: Thanks all — this should cut down onboarding friction a lot.
